rules: Use the existing coarse-first policy for acquisition, preserving its raw outcomes and status behavior.
If no valid route is obtained, return that failure without optimization.
If acquisition already returns a completed fine-graph path, do not perform a third search.
If a valid coarse path equals abs(goalX-startX)+abs(goalY-startY) in original world units, skip finer search; this bound applies to the declared axis-aligned model.
Otherwise run one fresh fine-graph search with the declared fine budget. A completed result may shorten or confirm the route.
If that optimization exhausts its budget, preserve the valid coarse route, expose raw failed optimization with empty/null fields and mark optimization incomplete.
Sum actual work from both stages. Report returned route source/spacing separately from last attempted spacing, and route validity separately from optimality evidence.
caps: At most two searches and coarseBudget+fineBudget=200 for quality-checked and original coarse-first; archived always-fine cap100. Known100-stage replay is not a general equal-total-budget comparison against always-fine.
replay: Exactly the30 archived original rows/endpoints/labels, no generation, filtering, replacement or new samples. This is a development-cohort replay after its two longer cases motivated the rule.

fallbackControl.scope: Separate AI known-case control, outside30-map summary. Expect retained length8 and failed optimization, not completed optimality.

validation: Full policy regressions; compare acquisition stages exactly to archived stages, new fine results to archived always-fine where budgets match, world geometry/masks/paths/BFS evidence and full cost accounting. Keep all raw prior failures immutable and distinguish fallback route success from optimization completion. Freeze source/protocol before replay.
attribution: Student selects objective2 only. AI formulates lower bound, rules, exact budgets/control, implementation, tests, operation and analysis.
scope: Known-cohort improvement/accounting, not held-out/generalization evidence, new cohort, actual workload, continuous global optimum, runtime/energy/storage or physical-robot result. Original baseline API/data/browser unchanged.
